page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 32 dedicated virtual CPUs across 16 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory is provisioned at 32.0 GB, establishing a strict 1 GB of RAM per vCPU ratio. The configuration contains no local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence, and includes no discrete GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a clear split between single-threaded and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core performance falls in the lower quartile, registering scores of 1106.89 in stress-ng and 1001.0 in Geekbench, alongside slower single-threaded gzip compression at 19.05 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics perform within the median range, achieving a multi-core stress-ng score of 23616.79, a PassMark CPU score of 23037.68, and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8847.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 95.0 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 45.75 GB/sec for writes. Static web throughput averages 17.02 GB/sec, while Redis achieves 22.46 million SET operations per second.

With a resource footprint tilted heavily toward compute rather than memory capacity, the instance offers practical cost efficiency for horizontal compute jobs that do not exceed 1 GB of memory per thread. The lack of integrated local disks and modest single-core throughput make it less suited for transaction-heavy databases or latency-sensitive single-threaded tasks. Instead, the ecs.ic5.8xlarge is well positioned for multi-threaded compilation tasks, distributed data crunching, batch computing, and parallel CI/CD pipeline stages.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, paired with 32 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:1 vCPU-to-memory allocation. It includes no bundled local storage and features a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Without hardware GPU accelerators, computing relies entirely on CPU execution, including AVX-512 vector extensions. Benchmark results reflect a noticeable divergence in execution capability: single-core performance scores in the lower quartile across Geekbench and stress-ng tests, whereas multi-core compute, clang compilation, and ray tracing reach mid-tier levels. Memory bandwidth achieves 95.0 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 45.75 GB/sec for writes. The ecs.ic5.8xlarge is suited for parallel batch processing, distributed build tasks, and CPU-intensive computational jobs where memory density requirements remain low.
